AMMI analysis of a multi-environment trial

Source: R/breeding.R
ammi.Rd

Additive main effects and multiplicative interaction model (Gollob 1968; Gauch 1988): the analysis of variance of genotypes and environments, and the singular value decomposition of the genotype x environment interaction into principal axes (IPCA), each tested with the degrees of freedom of Gollob (1968).

Usage

ammi(
  data,
  response,
  genotype,
  environment,
  block = NULL,
  mse = NULL,
  df_error = NULL,
  reps = 1,
  n_axes = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame in long format.

response

Name of the numeric response column.

genotype, environment

Names of the genotype and environment columns.

block

Optional name of the block (replicate) column; blocks are taken as nested within environments.

mse, df_error

Error mean square (plot scale) and its degrees of freedom, only when the data hold one mean per cell.

reps

Number of replicates behind each mean, when the data hold one mean per cell.

n_axes

Number of interaction axes shown in the analysis of variance (the rest is pooled as the residual interaction); by default all of them.

Value

An object of class "ad_ammi": the analysis of variance (anova), the interaction axes (axes: singular value, sum of squares, percentage of the interaction, Gollob degrees of freedom and F test), genotype and environment means with their scores (genotypes, environments, the first with ASV and YSI), the table of means and the interaction residuals.

Details

The data must be balanced: every genotype in every environment with the same number of replicates. With plot data the error comes from the trial itself (with block, blocks within environments are taken out and environments are tested against them). With one mean per cell, give the pooled error of the trial (mse, on the plot scale, with df_error) and the number of replicates behind each mean (reps).

Interaction scores are scaled by the square root of the singular values (symmetric scaling), so that the product of a genotype score and an environment score is their interaction. The sign of every axis is fixed so that the environment with the largest absolute score is positive. The AMMI stability value (ASV) of Purchase et al. (2000) is sqrt((SS1 / SS2 * IPCA1)^2 + IPCA2^2); the yield stability index (YSI) adds its rank to the rank of the mean (highest mean = 1).

References

Gollob, H. F. (1968) Psychometrika 33, 73-115. Gauch, H. G. (1988) Biometrics 44, 705-715. Purchase, J. L., Hatting, H. and van Deventer, C. S. (2000) South African Journal of Plant and Soil 17, 101-107.

Examples

fit <- ammi(maize_met, "Yield_t_ha", "Hybrid", "Environment", block = "Block")
fit
